title: Microsoft Purview: sensitivity label groups replace parent labels (Worldwide)
summary: The migration behaviour, licensing statements, admin paths and commands are supported by the roadmap records and Microsoft documentation. A minor checklist-to-table mismatch remains: the checklist asks administrators to edit label settings and check advanced settings, but the table does not cover those controls.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes a simplified scheme of labels and label groupings for organisation previously done with parent labels.
claims.quote: the sensitivity labeling scheme will be simplified to only consist of labels and label groupings. These new label groupings allow admins to better organize and categorize their labels (previously done via parent labels).

claims.claim: Label groups are replacing parent labels.
claims.quote: To reduce this complexity, label groups are now replacing parent labels.

claims.claim: Label groups look and behave the same to users.
claims.quote: Label groups look and behave the same to users

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Label groups support only name, descriptions, colour and priority rather than content protection settings.
claims.quote: have configuration options only for the settings that they support: the label name, descriptions, color, and priority.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Label groups themselves cannot be published, only the labels inside them.
claims.quote: You can't publish label groups themselves, only the labels within the groupings.

claims.claim: Microsoft calls the migrated organisation the modern label scheme.
claims.quote: In both these cases, your sensitivity labels will automatically use the modern label scheme

claims.claim: Migration is automatic for new tenants beginning October 1, 2025.
claims.quote: Migration is automatic if you have a new tenant beginning October 1, 2025

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Scope; Risk assessment
claims.claim: Migration is also automatic when it will not create a same-name sublabel.
claims.quote: Migration is automatic if you have a new tenant beginning October 1, 2025 or the migration of parent labels won't create a new sublabel with the same name because you have applicable parent labels.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Scope: Rollout
claims.claim: Outside the automatic cases, the documented migration is administrator-started from the banner and Migrate button.
claims.quote: To migrate your parent sensitivity labels to sensitivity label groups, use the Microsoft Purview portal if you see the information banner displayed in the following instructions. ... When you're ready to migrate your labels, select the Migrate button.

claims.claim: Migration is gradually rolling out and its banner may not yet be available to a tenant.
claims.quote: Migration is gradually rolling out, so migrating your parent labels to label groups might not yet be available for your tenant.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; controls[0].note; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Label migration is irreversible.
claims.quote: Label migration is irreversible.

claims.claim: The migration UI route is Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > Migrate to the modern label scheme > Get started > Review new scheme > New label scheme > Migrate.
claims.quote: Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels ... From this banner, select Get started ... select the Review new scheme button ... The New label scheme page ... select the Migrate button.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; What's changing; Governance guidance; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Label groups are created in the Microsoft Purview portal at Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > + Create > Label group.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels ... Select + Create and then Label group to start the new label group configuration.

claims.claim: The documented label-group creation route belongs to the modern label scheme.
claims.quote: Modern label scheme ... If you want to group your labels so that they display together vertically for users, first create a label group.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The Move into group action moves an existing label into a label group.
claims.quote: To move a label into the label group, first select the label and select ... for Actions. Select Move into group and select the required label group.

claims.claim: Administrators can create labels directly inside a group.
claims.quote: To create a new label for that group, first select the label group and then select ... for Actions. Select Create label in group to start the new sensitivity label configuration.

claims.claim: A parent configured for encryption, content marking, auto-labelling or PowerShell advanced settings is applicable for new-sublabel creation.
claims.quote: It's configured for label actions that include encryption, content marking, auto-labeling, and PowerShell advanced settings.

claims.claim: A parent in a different publishing policy from its sublabels is applicable for new-sublabel creation.
claims.quote: It's included in a different publishing policy from its sublabels.

claims.claim: The documented scope differences between a parent and its sublabels can cause new-sublabel creation.
claims.quote: A sublabel is configured for a label scope that the parent label isn't configured for. ... Within the same label policy, the parent label has one or more scopes that aren't configured for any of its sublabels.

claims.claim: The new sublabel has the original parent's name.
claims.quote: The resulting sublabel that's created has the same name, label GUID, and settings as the original parent label.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The new sublabel inherits the parent's GUID, preserving that GUID's reference to the migrated label.
claims.quote: Because label GUIDs are unique in your tenant, they are used by backend services and configurations to reliably identify a sensitivity label. ... the new sublabel inherits the GUID from the applicable parent label

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The new sublabel retains the parent's settings.
claims.quote: The resulting sublabel that's created has the same name, label GUID, and settings as the original parent label.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: The migrated label group gets a new GUID.
claims.quote: the new label group is given a new GUID.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Without reconfiguration, a same-name sublabel becomes selectable where its parent previously could not be selected.
claims.quote: Without reconfiguration, this new sublabel will be available to select in a policy where previously it couldn't be selected as a parent label.

claims.claim: Applying a label enforces its protection settings on content.
claims.quote: Then, end users apply labels to emails and documents. Finally, Office or third-party apps/services enforce protection based on the applied labels.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends specifying GUIDs rather than label names for advanced settings.
claims.quote: For example, we recommend you use the GUID rather than the label name to configure advanced settings.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The New label scheme page flags naming conflicts to resolve before migration.
claims.quote: This page will also alert you to any naming conflicts that need to be resolved before the migration.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Sublabel names must differ from their parent label's name.
claims.quote: All sublabels must have a unique name from their parent label.

claims.claim: The proposed New label scheme can be downloaded as a CSV for review before migration.
claims.quote: You can use the Download button to save a copy to a CSV file. The default name is NewLabelSchemecsv.csv.

claims.claim: Changing unnecessary parent-label actions and restarting review can reduce unnecessary same-name sublabels.
claims.quote: After making changes, restart the migration and check the post-migration information again from this page. ... Label actions are one of the reasons why migration creates a new sublabel that you might not need.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends testing migration in a test tenant with the same label configurations.
claims.quote: We highly recommend that you first test the migration by using a test tenant that has the same sensitivity label configurations as your production tenant.

claims.claim: The optional unpublishing process runs Script One in Security & Compliance PowerShell before migration and keeps that session open.
claims.quote: These PowerShell commands use Security & Compliance PowerShell. ... Script One: Before the migration, run the following command to fetch all policies that publish parent labels. ... Don't close your PowerShell session but keep it open during the label migration.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Script Two unpublishes newly created sublabels after migration completes.
claims.quote: Script Two: As soon as migration is complete, run the following script to unpublish the newly created sublabels from applicable parent labels:

claims.claim: A green message bar on Sensitivity labels confirms migration to the modern scheme.
claims.quote: you see a green message bar on the Sensitivity labels page that confirms your tenant is successfully migrated to the modern label scheme.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft says to allow up to 24 hours for migration as a precaution.
claims.quote: The migration process doesn't take long, typically just a few minutes to an hour. However, as a precaution, allow up to 24 hours.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft discourages label-configuration changes during migration because changes are likely to be lost.
claims.quote: While the migration is in progress, we don't recommend making any changes to the label configuration because those changes will likely be lost.

claims.claim: Sublabels in the same modern label group do not support the downgrade-justification setting.
claims.quote: If you're using the modern label scheme that replaces parent labels with label groups, sublabels in the same label group also don't support the justification setting.

claims.claim: Published labels are edited at Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies > policy > Edit Policy > Choose sensitivity labels to publish > Choose sensitivity labels to publish.
claims.quote: Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies. ... To edit an existing label policy, select it, and then select the Edit Policy button ... On the Choose sensitivity labels to publish page, select the Choose sensitivity labels to publish link.

claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy -Identity <policy> -RemoveLabels <label> unpublishes a label through Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: These PowerShell commands use Security & Compliance PowerShell. ... Set-LabelPolicy -Identity $policyToRemove -RemoveLabels $_

claims.where: Scope: Users; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Publishing policies determine which labels are made available to their selected users.
claims.quote: When you publish the label policy to your chosen users: The labels become visible to these users in their apps that support sensitivity labels

claims.claim: The Get started permissions section lists Information Protection, Information Protection Admins, Analysts, Investigators and Readers as role-group options.
claims.quote: You can use the following role groups: Information Protection; Information Protection Admins; Information Protection Analysts; Information Protection Investigators; Information Protection Readers

claims.claim: A custom role group containing Sensitivity Label Administrator is another management-permissions option.
claims.quote: Alternatively to using the default role groups, you can create a new role group and add the Sensitivity Label Administrator role to this group.

claims.claim: Compliance Data Administrator, Compliance Administrator and Security Administrator role groups are also documented options.
claims.quote: Another option is to add users to the Compliance Data Administrator, Compliance Administrator, or Security Administrator role group.

claims.claim: Label-management permissions are not required to apply labels in apps.
claims.quote: These permissions are required only to create and configure sensitivity labels and their label policies. They are not required to apply the labels in apps or services.

claims.claim: Built-in role-group membership is managed at Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups > Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions > role group > Edit > Edit members of the role group > Choose users.
claims.quote: Go to Settings > Roles and scopes ... Select Role groups. ... On Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions, select a Microsoft Purview role group ... Select Edit ... On Edit members of the role group, select Choose users or Choose groups.

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity "<role-group>" -Member "<user-UPN>" adds a user to a role group.
claims.quote: Use the Add-RoleGroupMember cmdlet to add members to a management role group. ... The Identity parameter specifies the role group to add a member to. ... The Member parameter specifies who you want to add ... User ID or user principal name (UPN)

claims.claim: The documented portal procedure for adding role-group members requires Role management.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal by using credentials for an admin account assigned the Role management role.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not state whether or when remaining banner-eligible tenants will eventually migrate without administrator initiation.
claims.quote: Searched: "label groups" "migration" automatic tenants deadline banner. Read migrate-sensitivity-label-scheme and create-sensitivity-labels; automatic cases and manual banner procedure are described, but no later forced-migration plan or date for other tenants was found.

claims.claim: The default is on for the automatic-migration cases, with administrator initiation separately qualified in the body.
claims.quote: Migration is automatic if you have a new tenant beginning October 1, 2025 or the migration of parent labels won't create a new sublabel with the same name because you have applicable parent labels.
